_meta.schema: same fields as kb/shared/learning-tools.json entries (name, role, licence, osi, version, released, mac, windows, install_mac, install_windows, lessons[], urls[]) plus maintained/notes as in the shared file
_meta.licence_note: Licences as read on 2026-10-29: SAOImage DS9 (Zenodo record + repo README), Stellarium and Siril (GitHub/GitLab repo licence), astrometry.net (README + Homebrew, which disagree on wording), TOPCAT (project page); JupyterLab copied from the shared catalog. See KNOWN-GAPS.

astronomy.name: Stellarium
astronomy.role: SEE / CHECK — planetarium: the sky for any place and time; replaces the telescope for position checks.
astronomy.install_mac: brew install --cask stellarium (cask 26.3 as read by the L300/L400 pass; macOS 11+, universal build)
astronomy.install_windows: winget install -e --id Stellarium.Stellarium (winget-pkgs folder exists; manifest version not read) or the installer from https://stellarium.org/ (Windows x86_64 Qt6, Windows 10+; ARM64 build listed)

lessons.exercise: Set Gurgaon (28.46 N, 77.03 E), 2026-10-29 21:00 IST, atmosphere off; find Polaris and Deneb.
Compare Deneb/Sirius Alt/Az with sky.py (56.27 deg / below).
Read JD 2461343.1458 and sidereal time ~23h10m at 15:30 UTC.
Check m - M = 5 log10(d/10 pc) for Deneb and Vega from the info panel.
Mars RA/Dec (J2000) on 2026-10-29 vs kepler.py (139.66 deg, +17.29 deg).
Compare B-V of Betelgeuse and Rigel with Wien peaks.
Watch Jupiter's moons: inner moons move fastest (Kepler's third law).
Set the location to Gurgaon (28.46 N, 77.03 E) and the time to 2026-11-24 18:50 IST; look at Sirius (below the horizon), Deneb (high in the north-west) and the full Moon next to Aldebaran.
Turn on the equatorial grid and compare RA lines 1 h apart near Orion (Dec -5) and near Cassiopeia (Dec +62).
Find pi Mensae (the real-data target of fetch_tess.py) from Gurgaon and from Sydney.

astronomy.notes: Needs OpenGL 3.3 (2.1 minimum). Licence: the GitHub repo shows GPL-2.0 (earlier pass recorded GPL-2.0-or-later from project pages).

astronomy.name: TOPCAT (+ STILTS)
astronomy.role: CHECK / SEE — interactive table viewer: sky pair matching, plots, phase folding.
astronomy.install_mac: brew install --cask topcat (DMG signed and notarized; also installs the stilts command)

lessons.exercise: Pair Match (Sky, 1 arcsec) on cat_a.csv/cat_b.csv: 1842 per-row, 1817 symmetric.
Phase-fold variable.csv at 0.5669 d vs the 1.3074 d alias.
VO > Table Access Protocol: connect to the Gaia archive TAP service and run the ADQL printed by adql_cone(83.82, -5.39, 0.05); then Joins > Pair Match (Sky, 1 arcsec) between two downloaded tables.
Open release/catalogue.vot (File > Load Table); look at Columns (units, UCDs). Then run: stilts votlint release/catalogue.vot
Load data/S01.csv (CSV) and plot flux vs time_d; add a column mod(time_d - 1.19, 3.1244) to see the folded transit.

astronomy.notes: Java 8+ (TOPCAT page). STILTS votlint validates VOTables (lesson 21).

astronomy.name: SAOImage DS9
astronomy.role: INSPECT — FITS image viewer with header and WCS readout.
astronomy.licence: GPL-3.0-only (Zenodo release record); repo README: GPL-3.0 'licensed in part'
astronomy.install_mac: Aqua .dmg (Apple-silicon port) from the DS9 download page; Homebrew cask saoimageds9 deprecated (fails Gatekeeper) and disabled since 2026-09-01
astronomy.install_windows: Installer from the DS9 download page (installs to C:\SAOImageDS9)

lessons.exercise: Open star_field.fits: header cards and WCS 5:35:17.30 -5:23:28.0 at pixel (32.5, 32.5).
Open master_flat.fits written by the lab (shipped run) with a linear scale; hover over the corners and the dust donut near x = 40, y = 32.

astronomy.notes: Download page notes a codesign step for the Mac app if macOS blocks it.

astronomy.name: AstroImageJ
astronomy.role: CHECK — aperture photometry and transit light curves with a GUI.

lessons.exercise: field.fits: aperture 6, annulus 10-15 on star 0 at FITS (31, 31): ~20006 e-.

astronomy.name: Siril
astronomy.role: BUILD WITHOUT CODE / CHECK — calibration (bias/dark/flat), stacking, photometry.
astronomy.install_mac: DMG from https://siril.org/download/ (macOS 13 Ventura or later)
astronomy.install_windows: Installer or portable build from https://siril.org/download/

lessons.exercise: Load master_flat.fits and open the Statistics dialog.

astronomy.notes: Siril 1.4.0 release notes: macOS < 13 support compromised; Intel Mac support may be dropped.

astronomy.name: astrometry.net (solve-field)
astronomy.role: CHECK — blind plate solver: writes a FITS WCS (.wcs) for a real image; the production version of lesson 14.
astronomy.licence: own code BSD-3-Clause; the whole work GPL-3.0-or-later (repo README); Homebrew lists BSD-3-Clause
astronomy.install_mac: brew install astrometry-net (+ index files for your image scale)
astronomy.install_windows: No native build: WSL2 (Ubuntu) sudo apt install astrometry.net (the project says 'it should work in WSL')

lessons.exercise: Solve any real image of yours (or a public-domain sky photo) with: solve-field --scale-units arcsecperpix --scale-low 1.8 --scale-high 2.2 image.fits, then read the .wcs header.

astronomy.notes: Needs index files matched to the image scale; Windows only via WSL2.

astronomy.name: JupyterLab (+ JupyterLab Desktop)
astronomy.role: CHECK / SEE — notebooks to re-run lab code step by step and plot results (same entry as ../../shared/learning-tools.json).
astronomy.install_mac: pip install jupyterlab, or Desktop arm64 installer
astronomy.install_windows: pip install jupyterlab, or Desktop x64 installer / winget install jupyterlab

lessons.exercise: In a notebook in this lab folder: from mcmc import *; post, acc, tau = run(tf.make_data()); plot histograms of post[:, 2] (T14) and post[:, 4] (ln s).
In a notebook: from solution.survey import *  (or load it by path); plot detect_s per unit from pipeline_metrics.jsonl for options A, B and C.
In a notebook: load solution/alerts.py by path, compute difference() for night 5 exposure a, and show it next to new - ref (shipped) with the same colour scale.
In a notebook: load solution/compare.py by path, fit the four models to galaxy.observed(), and plot the data with each model curve and the disk-only curve.
In a notebook in the capstone folder: from run_capstone import analyse_all; results, prov = analyse_all(); fold S01 at results['S01']['period_d'] and plot it; repeat for S05 at twice its period.

astronomy.notes: Facts copied from the shared catalog (checked 2026-10-28), not re-verified in this pass.
